What the Voat community fails to understand is that while it is important for a website like Voat to enable free speech, it doesn't preclude the subverses from having their own rules that dictate their own particular scope of discussion. And if they have those rules, they would need to be enforced by the mods. (Otherwise, why bother having mods in the first place?)

An example would be if you had a sub devoted to Sailor Moon that suddenly had users coming in and making posts about Dragonball Z. This threatens to derail the topic, and as such, the mods are well within their right to delete the DBZ content. This keeps the sub on their chosen topic.

Can mods abuse their power? Of course. And fortunately, Voat has a way to track deleted content, which ensures that anything the mods do is under scrutiny. If users start to see the mods are going too far, it's simple enough to start a new sub and move on. Likewise, if users feel that there should be a community that jointly addresses content (perhaps a Sailor Moon + DBZ community), they have the option to create that too.

Now v/ThePedes was created as a community for Donald Trump supporters coming from Reddit, and it seems that the stipulation was that racism and antisemitism would be kept to reasonable limits (avoiding political correctness, of course). Meanwhile, there's the previously-existing v/TheDonald community, which exists without those stipulations. Now it could be argued that these two should be combined, but it's clear that neither community desired that. (There were those willing to cross-pollinate, which is fine, but better that the two cultures be kept separate.)

There is nothing wrong with this arrangement, and in fact it would be beneficial for Voat in the long term, boosting the community and providing a way to strengthen one of the alternatives to the corruption of Reddit.

But instead of welcoming the newcomers, and being patient while they integrated, the Voat community was mostly hostile, attacking the community for restricting the scope of their content, among other minor quibbles. (And remember, Voat allows one to block communities, so the disruption could have been kept to a minimum.)

Of course, not feeling welcome, it seems that the newcomers aren't sticking around in great quantity. And it really does hurt Voat as a whole. Note that on v/ThePedes, there haven't been a number of substantial posts since the initial rush, and v/TheDonald is as lethargic as it's always been. Meanwhile, r/The_Donald is bustling with activity, despite the blatant censorship and corruption of Reddit.
